title: Email: Broker's Notice of Loss and the Audit Chair's Question

fields.cc: Priscilla Aranguren (General Counsel); Gareth Lindqvist-Boyd (Treasury Manager)
fields.subject: RE: Notice of loss – Tamarack – please sign
fields.body:
Marcus Delacroix-Hume, Anjali Whitcombe,

This confirms what I told you both by phone at 17:02.

Director Hollis Wetherbee-Ng, chair of the Audit Committee, has seen the Clipwave video and the Greenville Commerce Journal's questions. She asked me to put three questions to you:

1. Is it $2.6 million or $1.6 million?
2. Did we get any money back?
3. Does the committee need to meet tonight?

She wants one number she can rely on. She will not repeat a figure to the other directors until Finance has given it to her. She is available by phone until 21:00 tonight.

The broker's email below copied me. It asks for a signature tonight, and its figures don't match what I heard in the hallway. Please tell me which figures I should give the chair, and who will brief her.

Thanks,

-----Original Message-----
From: claims@harbourline-brokers.example
Sent: Tuesday, September 14, 2027 5:00 PM
To: Anjali Whitcombe (Controller); Marcus Delacroix-Hume (CFO)
Cc: Office of the Corporate Secretary
Subject: Notice of loss – Tamarack – please sign

Hello,

Following up on the loss, and to save you time, we have prefilled the carrier's Notice of Loss from what we've been told so far:

Type: social engineering / funds transfer fraud
Amount of loss claimed: USD 2,640,000
Recovered: USD 620,000
Date of discovery: 14 Sept 2027 14:05

Please countersign and return tonight so the panel counsel can be assigned. Underwriters still need the attestation we asked about at 16:42. The forensic panel firm also cannot start until we have the Workstation audit export.

Best regards,
Account Executive, Financial Lines
fields.signature:
Office of the Corporate Secretary
Tamarack Precision Components, Inc. | Greenville, SC
864-555-0109

instructorNote: This inject tests whether Finance sends back the broker's prefilled form, which counts the amount requested as the loss and the frozen funds as recovered. The team should instead sign the TPC-FIN-04 Section 7 reconciliation: requested $2,640,000, released $2,250,000, stopped $390,000, frozen $620,000, recovered $0, with the elapsed time from the first release at 10:55 to the bank call at 14:20. Then the CFO should brief the Audit Committee chair with that one figure within 24 hours, and Legal should send the written insurer notice. Decision point: the Controller and CFO decide which figures, discovery date and committee action go out tonight.
